task.description:
REWORK 2 of the ISS-0440 fix design. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gated: item 2 (the --dir override and the AC1 demonstration) PASSED with no defects and is SETTLED -- do not touch it. Two BLOCKERs remain, both narrow. This is a truth-in-claims fix plus one safety guard; neither mechanism changes shape.

BLOCKER 1 -- THE SECOND-ORDER OVERCLAIM. Your rework correctly withdrew the Mechanism B overclaim. But the REPLACEMENT claim reproduces the same error one level down. Sections 3.5/AC1 now say 'structurally impossible to merge... because nothing bypasses CI' and 'the violation would still be caught, every time, by Mechanism A at CI, before merge.' That is FALSE as stated, and both ORCH and the validator verified it independently:
  - `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow/branches/main/protection` returns 404 'Branch not protected'. main has NO branch protection: no required status checks, nothing.
  - PR #848, merged TODAY by this very session, has statusCheckRollup showing its two Backend gate runs as FAILURE and SUCCESS -- it was merged with a failing gate. ORCH re-confirmed this directly. That is a live counterexample in this repo's own history, not a hypothetical.
  So CI DETECTION is structural and unconditional (ci.yml:126 is a bare invocation, no if:, no continue-on-error -- that part of your claim is true and verified). CI BLOCKING A MERGE is NOT structural: it depends on the merging agent honoring the result, which is the same procedural character as the 1.3 claim you just withdrew.
  REQUIRED FIX: state the THREE tiers explicitly rather than two. (i) CI runs unconditionally -- structural, verified. (ii) A violation is therefore always DETECTED and recorded in CI output -- structural. (iii) Whether that detection BLOCKS the merge is procedural, because main has no branch protection and merges past red checks demonstrably happen. Then restate Mechanism A's guarantee in its true form: 'the violation is always detected and recorded', NOT 'the violation cannot reach main'. Correct every section that rests on the stronger reading, including AC1's own answer.
  DO NOT treat this as fatal to the design, and do not redesign anything. Unconditional detection plus two procedural enforcement points IS a real improvement over six prose-only mitigations that produced no detection at all. The design's value is not in question -- only the accuracy of how it describes itself. Say plainly what ISS-0440's title asks for ('structurally impossible') is NOT fully achievable in this repo's current configuration, and name what would achieve it (branch protection with a required status check) as out-of-scope repo administration. ORCH will file that as a follow-up issue; reference it as a known gap rather than silently leaving the title unmet.

BLOCKER 2 -- THE --dir FLAG'S OWN MISUSE SURFACE, UNGUARDED. The design never addresses two hazards its new flag introduces:
  (a) `--dir some/empty/or/wrong/dir` produces '0 violations, exit 0' -- indistinguishable from a genuine clean full-corpus run. Someone (or some agent) could run a scoped lint, see green, and believe the corpus is clean. Specify a guard. Options, none prescribed: refuse a directory yielding zero discovered files (non-zero exit, named reason); and/or always emit a loud banner naming the scanned directory and the discovered file count, so a scoped run can never be mistaken for a full one. A banner alone may suffice if it is unmissable -- your call, but justify it.
  (b) `--autofix --dir <real corpus>` is an unreviewed mass-rewrite surface. State what happens there and whether it is restricted. Note the corpus is currently CLEAN (1900 files, zero bad values), so a mass rewrite would be a no-op today -- but that is a fact about today, not a safety property.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: item 2 is settled -- the --dir threading, resolve_dir/1's default, the byte-identical no-flag path, section 5's demonstration, and the rejected inside-handoffs/ alternative all stand as written. Both mechanisms keep their shape. The four-option verdicts, the hook rejection, AC3/AC4/AC5 and the corrected corpus figure all stand. Design only, no implementation code. Update the design in place, complete this handoff, commit both to feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903. rework_count 2 of max 3 -- last before ORCH must escalate, so make the tier statement complete and unambiguous.
